Winery

Quinta do Vale Meão

Douro Superior estate created by Dona Antónia Adelaide Ferreira at the end of the nineteenth century, which her descendants, the Olazabal family, turned into their own winery from the 1999 vintage.

Quinta do Vale Meão lies in the Douro Superior, near Vila Nova de Foz Côa, on a great bend of the river Douro. It was the last great estate created by Dona Antónia Adelaide Ferreira, the celebrated nineteenth-century Port businesswoman, who bought land that was then almost uninhabited and turned it into an extensive vineyard. For decades the estate remained in the hands of her descendants.

For much of the twentieth century the grapes from Vale Meão were sold to the Ferreira house and were one of the sources of Barca Velha, the Douro’s historic red. In the late 1990s, Francisco Javier de Olazabal, a descendant of Dona Antónia and for years head of the Ferreira house, decided to make wine under the quinta’s own label. The first vintage was 1999.

The estate combines schist, granite and alluvial deposits by the river, a diversity uncommon in the Douro that is put to use in the blends. Traditional varieties are grown, such as Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz (Tempranillo), Tinta Barroca and Sousão. Part of the fruit is still trodden in granite lagares.

The house makes a main red, Quinta do Vale Meão, a second wine called Meandro, whites and Vintage Port. Today the project is run by the Olazabal family, with the involvement of the next generation.
